steps.say: 14 min back to the station. Aim to be on the platform by 10:36.

steps.title: Train to Weimar
steps.say: 14 minutes, straight through.

steps.title: You are in Weimar
steps.say: 2 h 2 min here, until the 12:52 on. Fifteen minutes downhill into the centre.

steps.title: Marktplatz
steps.move: Take the 8 — 23 min, instead of 29 on foot.
steps.say: Town hall and the Cranach house, with the old Elephant hotel.

steps.title: Theaterplatz
steps.say: The Goethe and Schiller statue stands in front of the theatre.

steps.title: Back to Bahnhof Weimar
steps.say: 20 min back to the station. Aim to be on the platform by 12:52.

steps.title: Train to Berlin
steps.say: 265 minutes and 2 changes — RE16, then S8, then RE3.

steps.title: You are in Berlin
steps.say: This is where you sleep tonight. You have arrived. Berlin Hauptbahnhof.

steps.title: Gendarmenmarkt
steps.move: Take the U5 — 25 min, instead of null on foot.
steps.say: Two matching cathedrals and the concert hall. The handsomest square in Berlin.

steps.title: Brandenburg Gate
steps.say: The obvious one, and still worth standing in front of.

steps.title: Museum Island
steps.move: Take the S2 — 18 min, instead of 24 on foot.
steps.say: Five museums on one island. The Pergamon's Ishtar Gate is the highlight.

steps.title: Berlin Cathedral
steps.say: Climb to the dome walkway for the view over the island.

steps.title: Goodnight, Berlin
steps.say: You made it. Berlin.

mittenwald/Leutaschklamm.note: Gorge walkway on steel catwalks over the water. 4 km from town.

seefeld/Seekirchl.name: Seekirchl

ettal/Abbey shop and distillery.note: The monks' liqueur, beer and cheese, sold at the gate.

ettal/Schloss Linderhof.name: Schloss Linderhof
ettal/Schloss Linderhof.note: Ludwig II's small palace with the golden bedroom. Bus from Ettal.

oberammergau/Dorfstraße.name: Dorfstraße
oberammergau/Dorfstraße.note: The main street, painted end to end.

oberammergau/Ammer riverside.name: Ammer riverside

murnau/Obermarkt.note: A colourful main street the Blaue Reiter painters put on canvas.

murnau/Münter House.note: Where Kandinsky and Gabriele Münter lived and painted. Still furnished.

murnau/Staffelsee.name: Staffelsee

munich/Nymphenburg Palace.note: Summer palace and park, 20 min by tram.

donauworth/Käthe Kruse Doll Museum.note: In an old monastery. Charming and odd.

nuremberg/Sebalduskirche.note: The older of the two great churches, below the castle.

nuremberg/Tiergärtnertorplatz.note: The square below the castle where everyone sits out.

nuremberg/Heilig-Geist-Spital.name: Heilig-Geist-Spital
nuremberg/Heilig-Geist-Spital.note: A hospital built out over the river on arches.

nuremberg/Imperial Castle.name: Imperial Castle

nuremberg/Hauptmarkt.name: Hauptmarkt
nuremberg/Hauptmarkt.note: The broad market square below the castle rock.

nuremberg/Albrecht Dürer's House.note: Where Dürer lived and worked, just below the castle gate.

nuremberg/Weißgerbergasse.name: Weißgerbergasse
nuremberg/Weißgerbergasse.note: The prettiest surviving half-timbered lane in the city.

nuremberg/Henkersteg.name: Henkersteg

nuremberg/Frauenkirche.name: Frauenkirche
nuremberg/Frauenkirche.note: On the market square. The clock figures move at noon.

nuremberg/St Lorenz.name: St Lorenz

bamberg/Obere Brücke.note: The bridge the old town hall stands on.

bamberg/Little Venice.name: Little Venice

bamberg/Bamberg Cathedral.name: Bamberg Cathedral
bamberg/Bamberg Cathedral.note: Four towers, and the Bamberg Horseman inside.

bamberg/Schlenkerla.name: Schlenkerla
bamberg/Schlenkerla.note: Smoked beer, poured from the barrel. Tastes like bacon. Try it once.

bamberg/New Residence rose garden.name: New Residence rose garden

bamberg/Michaelsberg Abbey.name: Michaelsberg Abbey
bamberg/Michaelsberg Abbey.note: On the hill above, with a ceiling painted with 600 medicinal plants.

rothenburg/Marktplatz.note: Town hall tower is climbable — narrow stairs, big reward.

esslingen/Innere Brücke.name: Innere Brücke
esslingen/Innere Brücke.note: A medieval bridge with a chapel standing on it.
esslingen/Innere Brücke.photoFile: Esslingen a.N. - Altstadt - Innere Brücke - Ansicht aus SO von Maille (1).jpg

esslingen/Frauenkirche.name: Frauenkirche
esslingen/Frauenkirche.note: Gothic, with a filigree spire that took two centuries.

esslingen/The oldest timber houses.name: The oldest timber houses
esslingen/The oldest timber houses.note: The row on Webergasse dates from about 1267 — the oldest standing in Germany.

esslingen/Kessler Sekt.name: Kessler Sekt
esslingen/Kessler Sekt.note: Germany's first sparkling wine house, founded 1826, still in its vaulted cellar.

fulda/Fulda Cathedral.name: Fulda Cathedral
fulda/Fulda Cathedral.note: Baroque, over the tomb of St Boniface.

fulda/St Michael's.name: St Michael's
fulda/St Michael's.note: 9th century, one of the oldest churches in Germany, right beside the cathedral.

fulda/City Palace.name: City Palace
fulda/City Palace.note: Prince-abbots' palace, with a mirror cabinet.

fulda/Palace gardens and Orangery.name: Palace gardens and Orangery
fulda/Palace gardens and Orangery.note: Free to walk through, with the huge Floravase at the top.

eisenach/Wartburg.name: Wartburg
eisenach/Wartburg.note: UNESCO castle where Luther translated the New Testament in ten weeks.

eisenach/Bach House.name: Bach House
eisenach/Bach House.note: Bach was born in Eisenach. Live demonstrations on historic instruments.

eisenach/Market square.name: Market square
eisenach/Market square.note: Town hall, the Georgenkirche where Bach was baptised, and cafés.
eisenach/Market square.photoFile: Thuringia Eisenach asv2020-07 img28 Market Square.jpg

eisenach/Luther House.name: Luther House
eisenach/Luther House.note: Where Luther lodged as a schoolboy.

erfurt/Anger.name: Anger
erfurt/Anger.note: The wide shopping street between the station and the old town.

erfurt/Merchants' Bridge shops.name: Merchants' Bridge shops
erfurt/Merchants' Bridge shops.note: Thirty-two houses on the bridge, with workshops in the ground floors.

erfurt/Ägidienkirche tower.name: Ägidienkirche tower
erfurt/Ägidienkirche tower.note: Climb the tower at the end of the bridge for the best view of it.

erfurt/St Severi.name: St Severi
erfurt/St Severi.note: The five-spired church sharing the steps with the cathedral.

erfurt/Krämerbrücke.name: Krämerbrücke
erfurt/Krämerbrücke.note: A bridge with houses on it, lived in continuously since 1325.

erfurt/Domplatz.name: Domplatz
erfurt/Domplatz.note: Cathedral and St Severi side by side above a huge open square.

erfurt/Erfurt Cathedral.name: Erfurt Cathedral
erfurt/Erfurt Cathedral.note: Climb the steps. The Gloriosa bell inside is the largest medieval bell in the world.

erfurt/Petersberg Citadel.name: Petersberg Citadel
erfurt/Petersberg Citadel.note: Baroque fortress on the hill. Best place for sunset over the city.

erfurt/Fischmarkt.name: Fischmarkt
erfurt/Fischmarkt.note: Renaissance houses and the town hall. Dinner here.

erfurt/Augustinian Monastery.name: Augustinian Monastery
erfurt/Augustinian Monastery.note: Luther was a monk here for six years.

erfurt/Old Synagogue.name: Old Synagogue
erfurt/Old Synagogue.note: The oldest standing synagogue in Europe, with a hoard of medieval treasure.

erfurt/egapark.name: egapark
erfurt/egapark.note: Big garden park on the edge of town, if you want green.

weimar/Cranach House.name: Cranach House
weimar/Cranach House.note: The painter's last home, on the market square.

weimar/Wittumspalais.name: Wittumspalais
weimar/Wittumspalais.note: Anna Amalia's town palace, where the salon met.

weimar/Goethe's Garden House.name: Goethe's Garden House
weimar/Goethe's Garden House.note: In the park by the river. Where he lived first.

weimar/Goethe's House.name: Goethe's House
weimar/Goethe's House.note: On Frauenplan. He lived here for fifty years; it is exactly as he left it.

weimar/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
weimar/Marktplatz.note: Town hall and the Cranach house, with the old Elephant hotel.

weimar/Park an der Ilm.name: Park an der Ilm
weimar/Park an der Ilm.note: Landscape park along the river, with Goethe's garden house in it.

weimar/Bauhaus Museum.name: Bauhaus Museum
weimar/Bauhaus Museum.note: The Bauhaus started in this town in 1919.

weimar/Duchess Anna Amalia Library.name: Duchess Anna Amalia Library
weimar/Duchess Anna Amalia Library.note: The oval rococo hall. Timed tickets, limited numbers, book ahead.

weimar/Theaterplatz.name: Theaterplatz
weimar/Theaterplatz.note: The Goethe and Schiller statue stands in front of the theatre.

naumburg/Nietzsche House.name: Nietzsche House
naumburg/Nietzsche House.note: Where Nietzsche grew up and later returned, ill.

naumburg/Town walls and Marientor.name: Town walls and Marientor
naumburg/Town walls and Marientor.note: The last surviving double gate in Thuringia.

naumburg/Naumburg Cathedral.name: Naumburg Cathedral
naumburg/Naumburg Cathedral.note: UNESCO. The twelve founder statues — Uta especially — are extraordinary.

naumburg/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
naumburg/Marktplatz.note: Late-Gothic town hall and burgher houses.

naumburg/St Wenceslas.name: St Wenceslas
naumburg/St Wenceslas.note: Has a Hildebrandt organ that Bach himself tested in 1746.

naumburg/Saale-Unstrut wine.name: Saale-Unstrut wine
naumburg/Saale-Unstrut wine.note: The northernmost quality wine region in Europe.

quedlinburg/Old town.name: Old town
quedlinburg/Old town.note: UNESCO. Around 1300 half-timbered houses from six centuries.
quedlinburg/Old town.photoFile: Quedlinburg asv2018-10 img04 pano from Muenzenberg.jpg

quedlinburg/Schlossberg and collegiate c.name: Schlossberg and collegiate church
quedlinburg/Schlossberg and collegiate c.note: Romanesque church on the castle rock, with the Ottonian treasury.

quedlinburg/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
quedlinburg/Marktplatz.note: Renaissance town hall with a Roland statue in front.

quedlinburg/Finkenherd.name: Finkenherd
quedlinburg/Finkenherd.note: The oldest corner of town, below the castle rock.

quedlinburg/Half-timbered museum.name: Half-timbered museum
quedlinburg/Half-timbered museum.note: In a house from about 1310 — one of the oldest in Germany.

wernigerode/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
wernigerode/Marktplatz.note: The town hall with two pointed towers, built for a merchant and never finished as one.

wernigerode/Breite Straße.name: Breite Straße
wernigerode/Breite Straße.note: The main street of painted half-timbered houses, including the Krummelsches Haus.

wernigerode/Wernigerode Castle.name: Wernigerode Castle
wernigerode/Wernigerode Castle.note: On the hill above the town. Twenty minutes up, or the little Bimmelbahn road train.

wernigerode/Kleinstes Haus.name: Kleinstes Haus
wernigerode/Kleinstes Haus.note: Three metres wide. People lived in it until 1976.

wernigerode/Harzquerbahn.name: Harzquerbahn
wernigerode/Harzquerbahn.note: Steam narrow-gauge from the town station. The Brocken train takes most of a day.

wernigerode/Schiefes Haus.name: Schiefes Haus
wernigerode/Schiefes Haus.note: A leaning mill house, propped up and still standing.

wernigerode/Lustgarten.name: Lustgarten
wernigerode/Lustgarten.note: The terraced garden below the castle, free and quiet.
wernigerode/Lustgarten.photoFile: Wernigerode später Frühling im Lustgartens von Wernigerode im Harz Foto 2005 Wolfgang Pehlemann Wiesbaden PICT0037.jpg

thale/Bodetal.name: Bodetal
thale/Bodetal.note: The deepest gorge north of the Alps. The path in from the station is flat.

thale/Hexentanzplatz.name: Hexentanzplatz
thale/Hexentanzplatz.note: The witches' dancing floor on the cliff. Cable car up from the valley.
thale/Hexentanzplatz.photoFile: Ein sonniger Anblick zum Hexentanzplatz vom Seilbahn in Thale (Naturschutzgebiet Bodetal).jpg

thale/Rosstrappe.name: Rosstrappe
thale/Rosstrappe.note: The rock with the hoofprint, opposite the Hexentanzplatz. Chairlift or a stiff walk.

halberstadt/Halberstadt Cathedral.name: Halberstadt Cathedral
halberstadt/Halberstadt Cathedral.note: Gothic, with a cathedral treasury of medieval textiles that has no equal in Europe.

halberstadt/Domplatz.name: Domplatz
halberstadt/Domplatz.note: Cathedral and the Liebfrauenkirche facing each other across the green.

halberstadt/Fischmarkt.name: Fischmarkt
halberstadt/Fischmarkt.note: The rebuilt half-timbered centre, with the Rathaus and Roland.

halberstadt/As Slow as Possible.name: As Slow as Possible
halberstadt/As Slow as Possible.note: A John Cage organ piece in the Burchardikirche, playing since 2001. It ends in 2640.
halberstadt/As Slow as Possible.about: Organ²/ASLSP is a musical piece by John Cage and the subject of the second-longest-lasting musical performance yet undertaken. Cage wrote it in 1987 for organ, as an adaptation of his 1985 composition ASLSP for piano.

halle/Marktplatz and the Red Tower.name: Marktplatz and the Red Tower
halle/Marktplatz and the Red Tower.note: Five towers over one square — four on the church, one standing alone.

halle/Market Church.name: Market Church
halle/Market Church.note: Luther preached here; his death mask is upstairs.

halle/Händel House.name: Händel House
halle/Händel House.note: Handel was born in this house in 1685. Instruments of his time, played.

halle/Moritzburg.name: Moritzburg
halle/Moritzburg.note: A ruined castle roofed in glass and aluminium, holding the modern art.

halle/Giebichenstein Castle.name: Giebichenstein Castle
halle/Giebichenstein Castle.note: On the cliff above the Saale, twenty minutes north by tram 7.

halle/Halloren chocolate.name: Halloren chocolate
halle/Halloren chocolate.note: The oldest chocolate works in Germany, 1804, with a room made of chocolate.

wittenberg/Castle Church.name: Castle Church
wittenberg/Castle Church.note: The door where the 95 theses went up in 1517. UNESCO, and the reason for the town.

wittenberg/Town Church of St Mary.name: Town Church of St Mary
wittenberg/Town Church of St Mary.note: Where Luther actually preached, with Cranach's altarpiece.

wittenberg/Luther House.name: Luther House
wittenberg/Luther House.note: The monastery he lived in for 35 years — the largest Reformation museum there is.

wittenberg/Melanchthon House.name: Melanchthon House
wittenberg/Melanchthon House.note: The quieter scholar next door, in a Renaissance house with its garden.

wittenberg/Markt and the Cranach houses.name: Markt and the Cranach houses
wittenberg/Markt and the Cranach houses.note: Town hall, the two statues, and the painter's courtyards behind the square.

wittenberg/Luther's Oak.name: Luther's Oak
wittenberg/Luther's Oak.note: Where he burned the papal bull in 1520. Five minutes east of the Lutherhaus.

magdeburg/Magdeburg Cathedral.name: Magdeburg Cathedral
magdeburg/Magdeburg Cathedral.note: The first Gothic cathedral on German soil, on the Elbe.

magdeburg/Green Citadel.name: Green Citadel
magdeburg/Green Citadel.note: Hundertwasser's last building. Pink, wonky, full of trees.

magdeburg/Elbe promenade.name: Elbe promenade
magdeburg/Elbe promenade.note: River walk between the cathedral and the bridges.

magdeburg/Monastery of Our Lady.name: Monastery of Our Lady
magdeburg/Monastery of Our Lady.note: Romanesque monastery, now a sculpture museum.

berlin/Brandenburg Gate.name: Brandenburg Gate
berlin/Brandenburg Gate.note: The obvious one, and still worth standing in front of.

berlin/Gendarmenmarkt.name: Gendarmenmarkt
berlin/Gendarmenmarkt.note: Two matching cathedrals and the concert hall. The handsomest square in Berlin.

berlin/Museum Island.name: Museum Island
berlin/Museum Island.note: Five museums on one island. The Pergamon's Ishtar Gate is the highlight.
berlin/Museum Island.about: The Museum Island is a museum complex on the northern part of Spree Island in the historic heart of Berlin, Germany. It is one of the capital's most visited sights and one of the most important museum sites in Europe.

berlin/Reichstag dome.name: Reichstag dome
berlin/Reichstag dome.note: Free, but you must register online in advance.

berlin/Berlin Cathedral.name: Berlin Cathedral
berlin/Berlin Cathedral.note: Climb to the dome walkway for the view over the island.

berlin/Memorial to the Murdered Jews of.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
berlin/Memorial to the Murdered Jews of.note: 2711 concrete slabs. Walk into the middle of it.

berlin/Tiergarten.name: Tiergarten
berlin/Tiergarten.note: The big central park, with the Victory Column in the middle.

berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.name: Alexanderplatz TV Tower
berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.note: 368 m. Book a time slot to skip the queue.
berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.about: The Fernsehturm in central Berlin was constructed between 1965 and 1969 by the government of the German Democratic Republic as both a functional broadcasting facility and a symbol of communist power.

berlin/Checkpoint Charlie.name: Checkpoint Charlie
berlin/Checkpoint Charlie.note: The old crossing point. Busy and a bit tacky, but it is the spot.

berlin/Charlottenburg Palace.name: Charlottenburg Palace
berlin/Charlottenburg Palace.note: The largest palace in Berlin, with a big park behind it.

berlin/Hackesche Höfe.name: Hackesche Höfe
berlin/Hackesche Höfe.note: Eight linked courtyards of shops and cafés in Mitte.

friedberg/Marienplatz.name: Marienplatz
friedberg/Marienplatz.note: A long sloping square with the town hall at the top.

friedberg/Wittelsbacher Schloss.name: Wittelsbacher Schloss
friedberg/Wittelsbacher Schloss.note: The castle on the ridge, with the town museum inside.

friedberg/Herrgottsruhkirche.name: Herrgottsruhkirche
friedberg/Herrgottsruhkirche.note: Rococo pilgrimage church ten minutes east of the centre.

jena/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
jena/Marktplatz.note: The old market with the Hanfried statue in the middle.

jena/JenTower.name: JenTower
jena/JenTower.note: The round tower over the city; there is a viewing platform at the top.

jena/Botanical Garden.name: Botanical Garden
jena/Botanical Garden.note: One of the oldest in Germany — Goethe had a hand in it.

jena/Zeiss Planetarium.name: Zeiss Planetarium
jena/Zeiss Planetarium.note: The oldest working planetarium in the world, from 1926.

saalfeld/Fairy Grottoes.name: Fairy Grottoes
saalfeld/Fairy Grottoes.note: Old alum mine turned into the most colourful show cave in the world.

saalfeld/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
saalfeld/Marktplatz.note: Renaissance town hall and a ring of gabled houses.

saalfeld/Johanneskirche.name: Johanneskirche
saalfeld/Johanneskirche.note: Late-Gothic hall church in the middle of town.

saalfeld/Saalfeld town walls.name: Saalfeld town walls
saalfeld/Saalfeld town walls.note: Towers and gates still ringing the old centre.
